name: Rachel and the stolen teraphim
charge: Stealing her father’s images, and hiding them under her while she sat upon them
summary: Rachel stole the images that were her father’s, hid them in the camel’s furniture and sat upon them, and told her father she could not rise up before him, so he searched and found them not. Jacob, not knowing, had said that whoever was found with them should not live. No sentence for the theft is announced. The strange gods stayed hidden in the household until Jacob commanded them put away before Bethel, and the beguiling of the mothers from Eve to Rachel is the warning the record leaves.
offenseFull: When Laban went to shear his sheep, Rachel had stolen the images that were her father’s (Genesis 31:19). Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman that fears the Lord shall be praised: she was fine, and she was a thief (Proverbs 31:30). Laban’s own question, why he had stolen his gods, tells what house she came out of: an idolater of the line of Nahor, whose fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time and served other gods, and that is why the Most High had told Abram to get out from his country and from his kindred (Genesis 31:30; Joshua 24:2).

Jacob, who did not know that Rachel had stolen them, answered that with whoever his gods were found, let him not live, and invited Laban to search before their brethren (Genesis 31:32). She had taken the images and put them in the camel’s furniture and sat upon them, and said to her father, let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before you, for the custom of women is upon me; and he searched all the tent and found not the images (Genesis 31:34-35). Idolatry was carried hidden into the covenant household, and a lie covered it, and her own husband had unknowingly pronounced a sentence over her head.
judgmentFull: No sentence for the theft is recorded, and Jacob’s oath was spoken in ignorance. The images stayed in the camp. Before going up to Bethel, Jacob said to his household and to all that were with him, put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments; the strange gods were there because she had stolen them and hidden them, and she gave them up then, and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem (Genesis 35:1-4). Idolatry hidden in a household has to be put away before a man can stand at Bethel.

What followed was protection, not punishment: the terror of God was upon the cities round about, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob, for the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear him and delivers them (Genesis 35:5; Psalms 34:7). From Eve to Rachel the scriptures show how sin comes into a house through the household, for of the woman came the beginning of sin, and the warning left here is for the mothers of Israel to guard against the same beguiling (Ecclesiasticus 25:24). Rachel died in hard labour bearing Benjamin in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and Jacob set a pillar upon her grave (Genesis 35:16-20); the record does not name that death as the penalty for the theft, and it is not given as one. Delay is not acquittal.

text.text: And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father’s.
Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.
And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father’s house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?

And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.
With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.
And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.
And God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth–el, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto God, that appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments:
And let us arise, and go up to Beth–el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and all their earrings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
And they journeyed: and the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
And they journeyed from Beth–el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.
And it came to pass, when she was in hard labour, that the midwife said unto her, Fear not; thou shalt have this son also.
And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Ben–oni: but his father called him Benjamin.
And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth–lehem.
And Jacob set a pillar upon her grave: that is the pillar of Rachel’s grave unto this day.
And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father’s house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?
And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid: for I said, Peradventure thou wouldest take by force thy daughters from me.
With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
And Laban went into Jacob’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the two maidservants’ tents; but he found them not. Then went he out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.
Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.
And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.
